alexanderbathfalamorthethird: The new signaller is Otto Alexanderbat, once a clockmaker from Marrow Fen. The corporal asked if a clockmaker was any use in a trench. Otto Alexanderbat said he would find out.

The corporal found out Otto Alexanderbat used to be a clockmaker. Otto Alexanderbat has been doing two jobs ever since. On Day 3, Verdel Ridge passed to the Concord. Otto Alexanderbat wrote the name in his diary with unusual care.
Otto Alexanderbat (Concord) and Cyril "Doc" Zaboravljeni (Hegemony) ended up in the same shell hole at Lantern Hill. They stared at each other. Then each crawled home, and neither has told anyone.
Edmund "Hollow" Biwott and Otto Alexanderbat tried to invent a new card game. The rules only made sense once they stopped betting tobacco.
echoss_3: Day 5. The corporal put Gustav "Spark" Echoss beside a veteran and said to copy everything except the language.
jewnipers: Lucien Jewnipers unpacked a cracked shaving mirror at R-F17. A neighbour shifted a bag to make room without asking what it was.
The sergeant read out the order: Verdel Ridge has fallen, hold the line. Lucien Jewnipers looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.

Lucien Jewnipers was hit through the chest at R-F17. He is breathing. That is all the medic would say. Shot by Quentin "Shadow" Danny of the Concord (@sus.danny2.0). An orderly waved the bearers in: one bed, cleared and scrubbed. Lucien Jewnipers was lifted onto it in the hospital dugout. Lucien Jewnipers slipped away in the night. The orderly who sat with him says he was not afraid.
Clement Jewnipers put a cracked shaving mirror beside the bunk. Someone who had known Lucien Jewnipers helped clear the shelf without saying why.

Clement Jewnipers fired at a movement across the wire at R-F17. The man went down: Ulrich Gpt, badly wounded. Clement Jewnipers raised his head for a heartbeat too long at R-F17. The bullet only grazed him. He will not do it again. Shot by Teodor Deanc of the Concord (@deanc_67).
majormalpractice_626: Nobody saw Emil Majormalprac arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in S-F5, and a quiet machine gunner under it.
Emil Majormalprac ended a letter with 'nothing to report', then added half a page about the missing soap.

Clement Tsanev taught Emil Majormalprac to play the harmonica. The whole squad has asked them both, politely, to stop. A letter from home found Emil Majormalprac before the night shift. Emil Majormalprac folded it small and kept it close.
mateorekon: The quartermaster asked Cyril Mateorekon to sign for the blanket. He examined the blanket and asked whether the holes were included.
The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. Cyril Mateorekon was number 78. He still remembers how cold the colonel's glove was.
Cyril Mateorekon noticed regular flashes from a crack in an old stone wall. The position looks obvious enough to make him suspicious.

On sentry duty Cyril Mateorekon watched the wire for six hours. Twice he thought the wire watched back. The Concord hold Verdel Ridge now, and they can see straight into S-F9. Cyril Mateorekon has learned to walk bent double.
Cyril Mateorekon had been watching the same gap for an hour. When Nils Zczc crossed it, Cyril Mateorekon fired. Nils Zczc was grazed.
A shell burst in the trench at S-F9. Cyril Mateorekon was thrown against the wall and did not get up. The bearers came at a run.
tephydraws: By the time Bram Tephydraws reached S-F5, the war was 2 days old and had its own habits. He learned the first one within the hour: keep your head down.
A replacement turned out to be from Stoneyford too. Bram Tephydraws and the newcomer argued about the same bakery for half the night.
Casimir Toro of the Hegemony and Bram Tephydraws of the Concord watched a broken branch near Verdel Ridge all morning. Neither could risk assuming it was only a branch.
vinnie2shoes: After 2 days of war, R-F6 had a place for everything. On Day 3, the men rearranged a shelf to make a place for Albin "Tin" Shoes.

Albin "Tin" Shoes transferred to the runners. The men in R-F6 said they would miss him. He is only three dugouts away. Verdel Ridge is in Concord hands. Albin "Tin" Shoes watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
Karel Pavla and Albin "Tin" Shoes compared drawings of home. Both drawings included a kitchen table larger than the house.

Albin "Tin" Shoes and Leopold "Brick" Moovin carried a kettle through three narrow turns without spilling a drop. The applause at the end caused the accident. A letter from home reached Albin "Tin" Shoes before dusk. Albin "Tin" Shoes read it twice and slept a little easier.
